MRR is the monthly run-rate of the customers paying at the latest date (an annual plan ÷ 12, net of discounts; trials, paused and unpaid subscriptions out, past due in), not revenue; movements and retention compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over the 12 months to that date, and annual churn is measured on the customers paying 12 months earlier, never a monthly rate × 12. anomaly_alerts.description: Read as P&C insurance data (earned premium, loss ratio, incurred losses, policies, claims, severity (incurred per reported claim), written premium, retention rate, average written premium per term). Losses are reported (case-incurred: paid to date plus case reserves) as of the latest valuation, gross of salvage and subrogation, with no IBNR and no loss-adjustment expense, in nominal dollars with no trend applied; loss ratios use earned premium. Lines differ in mix and exposure units, so a total across lines is a mix of them. Oct 2026 is partial (data through the 26th) and is left out of period comparisons. The data has no valuation date; measured to its last date (26 Oct 2026), 2026 (10 months) and 2025 (22 months) are still developing: their losses (and, by policy effective date, their earned premium) will usually rise, so they are not final and not comparable with mature years. Gender is shown as a description only: rating or underwriting on sex is restricted or banned in several US states (NAIC Model 880, Colorado SB21-169), so no rate recommendation is made on it.

anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as HR data (headcount, FTE, separations, attrition rate, voluntary attrition, hires, average salary (current staff)). Headcount is the people in force at the latest date (contractors and agency workers out, interns and part-timers in); separations and hires are events (a rehire's exits count separately); attrition is separations ÷ the average of the month-end headcounts over the 12 months to that date. Pay and protected attributes (gender, ethnicity) are never shown for groups of fewer than 11 people. Gender is shown as a description only: hiring, firing or pay decisions on it are discrimination, so no recommendation is made on it; groups of fewer than 11 people are not shown. Ethnicity is special-category data (GDPR Art. 9): shown as a description only, never a recommendation about people, and never for groups of fewer than 11. Performance ratings describe groups here; they are never used to rank or predict individuals. Pay is annual base salary as recorded: part-time salaries are not full-time equivalents, so groups with more part-timers (often women) show lower pay than on a full-time-equivalent basis, which the unadjusted pay gap uses; pay is never shown for a group of fewer than 11 people.

anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as SaaS subscription data (MRR, ARR, paying customers, new MRR, churned MRR, logo churn). MRR is the monthly run-rate of the customers paying at the latest date (an annual plan ÷ 12, net of discounts; trials, paused and unpaid subscriptions out, past due in), not revenue; movements and retention compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over the 12 months to that date, and annual churn is measured on the customers paying 12 months earlier, never a monthly rate × 12. A customer who starts and leaves inside one month appears in no month-end figure. The cancellation date in this export is when a customer asked to cancel, not when the subscription ended: a subscription keeps paying until its end date (or a scheduled cancellation date). Some subscriptions are scheduled to cancel after the latest date: they are still paying and are counted until they end. On a subscription list, MRR is computed by the product from each subscription's price, seats, discount and billing interval, at today's price: expansion, contraction and revenue retention need monthly MRR snapshots and are not computed from it.

Read as SaaS subscription data (MRR, ARR, paying customers, new MRR, churned MRR, logo churn). MRR is the monthly run-rate of the customers paying at the latest date (an annual plan ÷ 12, net of discounts; trials, paused and unpaid subscriptions out, past due in), not revenue; movements and retention compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over the 12 months to that date, and annual churn is measured on the customers paying 12 months earlier, never a monthly rate × 12. A customer who starts and leaves inside one month appears in no month-end figure.
The cancellation date in this export is when a customer asked to cancel, not when the subscription ended: a subscription keeps paying until its end date (or a scheduled cancellation date).
Some subscriptions are scheduled to cancel after the latest date: they are still paying and are counted until they end.

On a subscription list, MRR is computed by the product from each subscription's price, seats, discount and billing interval, at today's price: expansion, contraction and revenue retention need monthly MRR snapshots and are not computed from it.
